column1: # Placement of WORKLIST_B.tsv (130 names) against the faceted models ontology.
# Classification pass, 2026-10-06. Rows are in worklist order.
# verdict: lineage | alias | generic | algorithm | quarantine | misextraction | unsure
# target:  parent node_id (lineage) or the node it spells (alias). `|` = R5 second parent.
# connectivity/topology/attributes: for `lineage`, what this node PINS -- only what
#   differs from its parent. For `generic`, everything the name alone pins.

column8: why
Settled algorithm-side (brief 2.1): a training objective over a flow network. The model is whatever backbone the paper names.
Brief 2 fixed point: PPO is an update rule; the model is the policy/value network.
Rainbow combines seven DQN improvements, all of them changes to the RL update rather than to the network.
Model-based RL agent: learned dynamics plus MCTS planning. The contribution is the training and search procedure; the networks are plain residual convnets. Same reading as AlphaZero.
Joint-embedding SSL objective (variance-invariance-covariance regularisation). The quote itself groups it with SimCLR and SwAV.
World-model RL agent. Its network is the RSSM, which is already the lineage node `rssm`; DreamerV2 contributes the imagination-based learning procedure. See notes.
Distributed actor-learner RL algorithm (V-trace off-policy correction).
Same referent as `proximal policy optimization (ppo)`; algorithm either way, so no alias row is needed.
Brief 2 fixed point: PPO/SAC/DQN are algorithms; the model is the Q-network.
Self-play plus MCTS training procedure over an unchanged residual convnet.
Settled algorithm-side: federated averaging is an aggregation/optimisation procedure.
R1: EleutherAI's open replication, introduced as GPT-3-like decoder LMs. Sibling of `gpt_neox`. Pins nothing -- self-attention, causal decoder and additive residual are all inherited.
R3 case 2: the long form of the declared acronym of `Segment Anything (SAM)`.
Twin Delayed DDPG: an off-policy RL update rule.
Actor-critic RL update rule.
SSL redundancy-reduction objective; the quote describes it purely as a loss. The model is the ResNet encoder.
Bare generic named in brief 4.7 alongside `neural networks`: uninformative, excluded from family shares, reported as a line.
R1 + R3: a separately named distilled release of HuBERT.

R1: Emphasized Channel Attention, Propagation and Aggregation in TDNN -- defined against the x-vector TDNN. Adds Res2Net-style dilated 1D convolutions and residual connections. Its squeeze-excitation channel attention is NOT pinned as connectivity, following `senet`, which pins nothing for the same mechanism; see notes.

The merge took `GAN` apart as a lineage root (lineage/nodes.tsv header): adversarial training is an objective. Named GAN architectures (DCGAN, StyleGAN, CycleGAN, SRGAN) stay as nodes. Not quarantine -- it names a definite paradigm, just not a model.
R3 case 2: long form plus declared acronym of `gat`.

R1: Nearest Neighbor Language Models -- a Transformer LM whose next-token distribution is interpolated with a kNN lookup over a datastore. The attributes axis lists retrieval-augmented models under `External memory`, which makes this model-side rather than a decoding trick.
A field-wide mass noun, excluded by the design exactly as `neural networks` is.
Settled algorithm-side (parameter-efficient fine-tuning). The connectivity axis's `Factorized / low-rank` names LoRA-shaped adapters, but the name denotes the tuning procedure, not a released model.
Momentum-contrast SSL objective; the quote calls it a pretraining method for detection backbones. The model is the encoder.
A library. Known case; belongs in libraries[], never in models[].

R1: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model pre-training -- a BERT-style masked LM coupled to a learned neural retriever over a document store. Pins only the memory attribute; the bidirectional encoder stack comes from `bert`.
Brief 2 fixed point.
Self-Predictive Representations: an auxiliary self-supervised objective bolted onto a Rainbow/DER agent, leaving the network unchanged.
R3 case 2. SPELLINGS.tsv already carries `vision transformers` and `vit (vision transformer)`; the bare singular long form is missing.

The string is a mangled `delta-model` -- the quote names "the delta-model, a tractable approximation to the distributional successor measure" and extraction dropped the leading Greek letter. As written it denotes nothing; it needs re-extraction before placement.
R1 + R3: XLM-R further pretrained on African languages; a separately named release.

R5 composite: a ViT image encoder and a BERT text encoder aligned contrastively ("Align before Fuse"), then joined by a cross-attention multimodal encoder. Pins mirror `vilbert`, the closest existing node.

The quote frames the named items as "PDA algorithms"; AR is Adversarial Reweighting for partial domain adaptation -- a reweighting/training procedure. See notes: the two-letter string is also a plausible mis-extraction of "autoregressive".
The quote itself calls it a framework that "a convolutional neural network integrated in" -- software tooling. The model is the unnamed CNN inside it.
Bayesian Causal Discovery by variational inference over DAGs. The named object is an inference scheme for a posterior over graph structures, not a separable architecture. Same reading as `dibs`.
The BIG-bench paper's name for Google's internal dense decoder-only Transformer LMs, reported as a size series. Sibling of the other dense LM families attached directly to `transformer`.

Big Transfer (BiT) ResNet-v2-101: a separately named release (R3), and the quote says so. Attached directly to `resnet` because the intermediate `BiT` node does not exist -- see notes; `BiT` would be descent, not grouping, so it is creatable, just not by me here.
A Byzantine-tolerant distributed optimisation method with variance reduction and compression. An optimiser, not a learned object.

Either Kim et al. 2016's character-aware LSTM language model (a named design, a node under `lstm`) or the LEAF benchmark's stacked-LSTM character LM used as a generic federated baseline. The quote fits both. If generic it pins gated-recurrence and single-component and nothing else.
Clipped stochastic extragradient: an optimiser. The quote gives the full name.
Clipped stochastic gradient descent-ascent: an optimiser.

The quote describes a combination, not a named release: "combines Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)". Pins the two connectivity values the name states; depth, widths and directionality stay unknown. See notes on the coarse/fine convention for generic rows.

R1: a Neural Process built from Constant Memory Attention Blocks. `Linear attention` is the nearest available value but is not exactly right -- the claim is constant MEMORY in the context size. See notes.

The string joins two systems with a plus (the Contriever retriever and the Atlas reader); it is a pipeline, not one name. It should be split before placement, and neither component exists as a node yet.
R3 case 1: a contracted spelling of "convolutional network", the canonical name of the `cnn` root. Not currently in SPELLINGS.tsv.
Certifiably Optimal RulE ListS. The learned object is a rule list; the branch-and-bound search is the algorithm. Same split as `xgboost`, which is a node under `gbdt` while boosting is the algorithm.
R1: a cross-attention ViViT over paired spatiotemporal streams (station series plus satellite context). Its literal R1 parent is ViViT, the video ViT, which is not a node -- see notes.
A GFlowNet over DAG structures; GFlowNet is settled algorithm-side.

Placed by precedent rather than conviction: `hubert` and `wavlm` are already nodes under `wav2vec2` though they too differ only in the SSL objective, and the quote treats data2vec as a released checkpoint family beside them. See notes.
Off-policy actor-critic update rule.
Same referent as DQN -- the quote glosses it "Deep Q-Learning (DQN)". Algorithm either way.

R1: Deep Speech / Deep Speech 2 is an end-to-end ASR stack -- a convolutional front end into bidirectional gated recurrent layers. The CTC loss is algorithm-side. Attached at the `rnn` root because no named recurrent ASR parent exists.
Data-Efficient Rainbow: a hyperparameter and algorithmic variant of Rainbow, as the quote spells out.
Differentiable Bayesian Structure learning: a variational inference procedure over graph structures.
Diffusion is settled algorithm-side; the model is the denoiser, a U-Net or a DiT.
R1 + R3: a separately named distilled release of GPT-2.

R5 hybrid, mirroring `deepfm`: embedding tables with a dot-product (low-rank) interaction feeding MLP towers. DLRM is framed as joining the collaborative-filtering and the predictive-analytics traditions, which is exactly those two parents.
A doubly-robust meta-estimator for treatment effects. It wraps arbitrary base learners; the contribution is the estimating equation.
DrQ(epsilon): data-regularised Q-learning, an RL algorithm. The string has lost its epsilon, but the quote identifies it unambiguously.
The quote calls it a hybrid planner. Planning is a sampling procedure over an unchanged world model.

A named E(3)-equivariant network that iteratively refines a ligand pose. Its R1 parent is most likely EquiBind, which is not a node, so I attached it at the family root instead of guessing an edge. Verify -- see notes.
Episodic Multi-agent RL with Curiosity-driven exploration: an exploration/training method, listed in the quote beside QMIX and MAVEN as a baseline.
Empirical risk minimisation is a training principle, not a model; the quote uses it to mean "trained with plain cross-entropy and no fairness constraint".

R5 composite: a ViT image encoder and a matching text encoder joined by a multimodal fusion encoder. The text tower is pinned to `transformer` rather than `bert` because FLAVA's text encoder is a ViT-architecture encoder, not a BERT release.

A SMILES sequence-to-sequence Transformer for retrosynthesis that fuses reaction-context embeddings. The quote calls it a framework but the named object is the model; the quote does not state its R1 parent.
R3 cases 2 and 3: plural long form with the acronym.
R1: GCN with Initial residual and Identity mapping. The residual path is precisely what it adds to GCN, and the quote names GCN as its baseline.

R1: a generalisation of directional message passing (DimeNet), by the same authors. Pins nothing -- `dimenet` already pins Euclidean equivariance. See notes: the quote calls GemNet INVARIANT, and the axis has no invariance value distinct from equivariance.
Same referent as `gflownet`; settled algorithm-side.
A GFlowNet-trained posterior over dropout masks: a regularisation/training method over an unchanged backbone.
An EM training framework alternating between a language model and a GNN. Both backbones are unchanged, which is the backbone test.

A separately named served release; the quote pins this instance to "Google Bard powered by Gemini Pro". Caveat in notes: Bard's backbone changed over time (LaMDA, then PaLM 2, then Gemini) and neither LaMDA nor PaLM 2 is a node, so this edge is true of the quoted release only.
R5 hybrid, and the quote states it outright: "a hybrid Message Passing Neural Network / Graph Transformer model". Its literal R1 parent is GraphGPS, which is not a node -- see notes.
R3: a separately named release.
EleutherAI's 6B GPT-3-class decoder LM; sibling of `gpt_neox` and `gpt-neo`. Explicitly NOT an alias of GPT-4 -- that is the known string-similarity defect.
R3 cases 2 and 3.
R3 case 2.
R3 cases 2 and 3.

Geometric Vector Perceptron network: message passing over protein structure with vector-valued features that rotate with the input. The quote uses it as a structure encoder beside GearNet and CDConv, neither of which is a node.
Offline RL update rule.
A MARL training scheme in which each agent learns its own Q-function. Note the acronym collision: two different algorithms in this worklist are both called IQL.
Implicit Quantile Networks: a distributional RL update rule.

Jointly-learned Exit and Inference for a Dynamic Neural Network. It adds learned exit gates to an arbitrary backbone, which is `Conditional / mixture-of-experts` on the routing attribute -- a model-side property -- yet it has no R1 parent and its contribution is a joint training scheme. Model or algorithm? See notes.
Brief 2 fixed point: k-NN has no separable learned object. Algorithm only.
A learning-to-rank gradient/loss; the quote itself says "LambdaRank Loss".
A multi-agent learning rule that differentiates through the opponent's update.
R3: a separately named release (size plus chat tuning). Brief 4.7 places `llama2-7b` exactly this way.
R3 case 1: the trailing "model" is orthographic.
R3 case 2: the extractor's `long form (ACRONYM)` shape, inverted.
A manifold-alignment procedure. Like t-SNE and PHATE it emits coordinates for the given points rather than a separable learned object, which is the k-NN / kernel-density case in brief 2.
Multi-Agent Variational Exploration: a MARL exploration algorithm.
Names a role -- a network whose input is another network's parameters -- not an architecture. The quote pins nothing on any axis. Borderline with quarantine; see notes.
Data augmentation; the quote says so in as many words.

The named object is an SE(3)-equivariant graph network over paired 2D and 3D molecular views; the SDE/diffusion machinery is algorithm-side under the backbone test. Attached at the family root because the quote does not name a parent.
m-POT: partial-optimal-transport domain adaptation. The quote groups it with the other "PDA algorithms".

The quote describes "our denoising transformer model" with an attention mechanism mixing 2D graph connectivity and 3D spatial information -- a Transformer variant. No further pin is safe from the quote alone.
NLLB-200: a sparsely gated mixture-of-experts encoder-decoder translation model. The distilled dense variants are separate releases that would re-pin routing back to the default.

Ordered Reliability Bits GRAND is a channel-decoding search procedure with no learned parameters at all, so it cannot be a model here. Flagged in notes -- the algorithms dimension may not want it either.
R1: equivariant message passing, introduced explicitly against invariant MPNNs such as SchNet. `mpnn` pins only permutation equivariance, so the Euclidean value has to be pinned here.
R1: a Transformer encoder over patches of a time series, channel-independent -- the same move ViT makes for images. Encoder-only, so the topology has to be pinned (the `transformer` root pins none).
A diffusion-based dimensionality-reduction procedure; no separable learned object. Same reading as t-SNE.
The Deep Planning Network agent: an RSSM latent dynamics model plus online MPC planning. `rssm` is already the node for the network; PlaNet contributes the planner. See notes, with DreamerV2.
Distillation is settled algorithm-side; the quote describes a joint representation/prototype learning objective.
An equivariant protein sequence-structure co-design network. The quote does not name its R1 parent; AlphaFold-style modules are the likely source. Verify -- see notes.
A proximal variant of LOLA: a multi-agent learning rule.
MARL value factorisation; the same bucket as DQN among the brief's fixed points. Caveat in notes: QMIX does specify a monotonic mixing network, so it is less purely objective-side than PPO.
A distributional RL update rule; the quote calls it an algorithm.
A decode-time procedure that builds uncertainty-aware suggestions from samples of an unchanged code language model.
An OOD-detection framework computed from an existing model's output distribution; it adds no learned object.
A module of a brachytherapy treatment-planning system -- software, and not machine learning at all.
A flexible architecture for token-efficient inference built on tree-structured retrieval, but the quote says neither what the architecture is nor what it derives from. Needs the paper.
R1: a Slot Attention variant -- the quote calls it an "object-centric architecture", and the MESH change is to slot attention's assignment cost.
Stepwise Adaptive Feature Norm: a domain-adaptation training method. The quote groups it with the "PDA algorithms".
R1, and the quote states it: "an unsupervised pre-training framework based on Masked Autoencoders (MAE)" for satellite imagery.
Successor features used to decouple LLM dynamics from task-specific rewards: a control/decoding procedure over an unchanged language model.

Cited as a specific baseline ("[18]") and the quote gives the architecture: two convolutional layers, each followed by max-pooling and dropout. Probably Schirrmeister et al.'s ShallowConvNet, the EEG baseline that sits beside `eegnet`. If the citation is spurious the name is a generic -- see notes.
SimCLR is settled algorithm-side; v2 changes the objective recipe, the projection head and the encoder size, not the model class.
Slow momentum: a distributed optimisation method, as the quote describes.
R3: a separately named release, and the quote contrasts it with 1.5.
A decoder-only code LM, attached at `transformer` like the other open LLM families (Mistral, BLOOM, Falcon, Qwen). See notes: `StarCoder`, fine-tuned from it, would be a child of this node.
R3: a separately named size variant of Swin Transformer. Size variants are nodes, not spellings.
A nonparametric embedding procedure: it returns coordinates for the given points and no separable learned object (brief 2, the k-NN / kernel-density case).

Temporal Graph Networks: message passing over a dynamic graph with a per-node memory vector updated by a GRU. The memory is an addressable store outside the parameters, which is the `External memory` test.

A named released toxicity classifier for game chat, but neither the name nor the quote states its backbone (reported elsewhere as a fine-tuned BERT/RoBERTa). R1 needs the paper's own framing, so I will not guess the edge.
R3 cases 2 and 3: plural long form of `Transformer neural process`.

R5 composite: a single-stream BERT-style encoder over the concatenation of text tokens and Faster R-CNN region features. Unlike `vilbert` it is ONE tower, so it pins neither cross-attention nor multi-tower; the inherited bidirectional encoder stack is right.

R1, and the quote says it: V-Net "leverages different types of backbones to the U-Net architecture" for 3D volumetric segmentation. A sibling of `unet_3d`, not the same design. Axes deliberately left empty: V-Net has BOTH U-Net concatenative skips and ResNet-style additive residuals, and `Shortcut connections` is single-valued within its family, so pinning additive-residual would silently delete the skips. See notes.

A three-stage latent-diffusion text-to-image architecture whose contribution is a far more aggressively compressed latent stage; R1 against latent diffusion, which is the `stable_diffusion` node's own canonical name. The three-stage cascade is not expressible on topology -- see notes.
R5 composite: a vision encoder and a text encoder joined by a cross-modal fusion encoder, aligned at multiple granularities. Same shape as `albef`.
